priority: FIRST: count leaflet pairs on ONE COMPLETE mature leaf (one pair versus many pairs).
SECOND: compare leaflet length-to-width ratio and outline.
THIRD: magnify hairs—soft velvet versus short backward-pointing hairs and stiff bristles.
FOURTH: find and photograph the extrafloral nectary near the leaf-rachis junction.
FIFTH: inspect the asymmetric flower, anthers, sepals, and mature pod.
Check pods and floral/seed structures before separating the look-alike broad two-leaflet species.
study_strategy.warning: Yellow flowers are NOT enough. S. roemeriana, S. pilosior and S. bauhinioides can all have a single leaflet pair. Kew and a 2024 flora disagree about the lifespan of S. pilosior, so don't identify it by annual versus perennial habit.
study_strategy.audience: Central Texas field crew visual ID; use magnified true-part photos with labeled pairs, gland, hairs and pods.
shared_traits: Fabaceae → Caesalpinioideae → Cassieae; this is a legume genus but its flowers are not shaped like the usual banner–wing–keel pea flower.
Leaves alternate; usually evenly pinnate (an even number of leaflets, with no lone terminal leaflet). Some local Senna have just ONE pair.
Look for an extrafloral nectary: a small nectar-producing gland near the petiole or between leaflet pairs. Its presence, position, and shape vary—do not assume every species has one.
Flowers commonly have five unequal yellow petals and stamens of unequal size; pollen is released through pores or short slits at anther tips.
Fruits are legume pods that may be flattened or cylindrical. Unlike many Chamaecrista, Senna pods do not spring open with strongly twisting valves.
Sennas vary from herbs to shrubs and trees worldwide; a low plant or tall plant alone does not settle its species.

quick_split: One leaflet pair with long narrow lanceolate leaflets (typically 2–9 times longer than wide): investigate S. roemeriana.

One pair of broader (approximately 1.3–1.8 times as long as wide) hairy leaflets and a mixture of short backward-pointing hairs plus conspicuous stiff setae: investigate S. pilosior (western comparison; RANGE UNRESOLVED).
One pair of oblong/obovate leaflets (often 1–2.5 cm long), very short thick style and rough seed coat: investigate S. bauhinioides (external comparison; not installed).
Usually 4–8 leaflet pairs, oval/oblong and densely velvety, robust perennial: S. lindheimeriana.
Many small leaflet pairs with a cup-like nectary near the base of the leaf plus rapidly splitting twisting pods: check Chamaecrista, especially C. fasciculata; not Senna.

decision_tree.question: How many pairs of leaflets on ONE mature compound leaf?
decision_tree.then: S. lindheimeriana candidate; check full hairy leaflet and reproductive macro.
decision_tree.else: Only one pair: proceed to step 2. Many pairs but not matching lindheimeriana: check Chamaecrista and other Senna.

decision_tree.question: Are the one-pair leaflets conspicuously long and narrow (about 2–9 times as long as wide)?
decision_tree.then: S. roemeriana candidate: confirm short leaf-junction nectary and flower/pod.
decision_tree.else: Broad leaflets: proceed to step 3; do not force roemeriana.

decision_tree.question: Are stems/leaflets strongly hairy with mixed stiff setae and short retrorse hairs?
decision_tree.then: S. pilosior candidate; confirm flower and erect hairy pod, and western provenance.
decision_tree.else: S. bauhinioides or another bifoliolate Senna candidate; get flower style + mature pod/seed evidence.

decision_tree.question: Is the broad-leaf bifoliolate plant difficult to settle vegetatively?
decision_tree.then: Do not guess. S. bauhinioides has stout distally dilated style and rough seed coat; S. pilosior requires hair, flower and fruit character confirmation.

comparison_lesson.confuser_warning: Yellow-flowered Rhynchosia and other Fabaceae can be deceptive; examine flower architecture before assigning genus. Rhynchosia senna is a different genus despite the epithet 'senna'.

curation_status.morphology_correction: Source conflict: Kew annual versus 2024 flora perennial for S. pilosior; do not key on life history.

look_here_first: Count PAIRS of leaflets on one entire leaf. ONE pair: inspect narrow versus broad leaflets and stem hairs. FOUR to EIGHT velvety pairs: think Lindheimer's senna. Then confirm the gland and pod. Yellow flowers come later.

shared_traits.lineage: Fabaceae > Caesalpinioideae > Cassieae > Senna; historical Cassia names may appear on specimens and older field guides.
recognition: Alternate, usually even-pinnate compound leaves without a lone terminal leaflet; some Senna species have just one leaflet pair.
Five unequal yellow petals, often with conspicuously unequal stamens and pore-opening anthers; do not assume a papilionaceous pea flower.
Legume fruits; shape, pubescence, posture, dehiscence, and mature seeds aid difficult IDs.
Small extrafloral nectary/gland often on petiole or rachis in or near leaflet pairs; location varies by species.
shared_traits.caution: Flower color, overall plant size, season, or hairiness alone cannot separate all Senna species. Not all legumes fix nitrogen; avoid claiming nodulation for these species without evidence.

field_practice.instruction: Present photographs of one mature complete leaf from S. roemeriana and S. lindheimeriana; require learner to mark the rachis and count leaflet PAIRS.
Pair equal-scale leaf closeups from S. roemeriana, S. pilosior and S. bauhinioides; label length:width ratios; add macro of stem hair types and leaf-junction gland.
Use flower closeups for style/anther separation and macro of both sides of mature pods; add seeds for S. bauhinioides.
Compare the petiolar nectary position, complete leaf, and mature dehisced pod of partridge pea.

Explain source difference: POWO annual vs 2024 morphological flora perennial for S. pilosior. Both accounts agree on one pair of comparatively broad leaflets. Teach reproducible observed structures, not habit assumptions.

scientific_guardrails.region: Hays County plus 23 named western/northern target counties in PROJECT_RULES.md; BONAP/NAPA preferred
scientific_guardrails.evidence_audit: The installed species records currently count Val Verde for S. lindheimeriana and Williamson for S. roemeriana. Neither county is in the 24-county project target-zone list. Current PASS labels must be rechecked for a third qualifying county before making three-county native-certified claims. Do not silently rewrite prior taxonomy/range approvals or manufacture replacement counties.
scientific_guardrails.admitted_vs_certified: All three species remain in the approved learner. S. pilosior is range-unresolved and not certified local native.
scientific_guardrails.taxonomy: Accepted Senna names; Cassia names in older sources are synonyms and not duplicate learner species.
scientific_guardrails.life_history_conflict: POWO: annual S. pilosior; 2024 peer-reviewed flora: herbaceous perennial. No categorical ID statement. Leave county range separate.
scientific_guardrails.no_assumed_nitrogen_fixation: Being a legume does not itself establish nodulation or useful soil nitrogen fixation for every Senna.
scientific_guardrails.range_current: roemeriana and lindheimeriana PASS labels have 24-county threshold evidence flags recorded in species pages; do not treat current evidence as fully repaired.
scientific_guardrails.flower_feature: Do not call Senna flowers ordinary banner–wing–keel pea flowers.
scientific_guardrails.genus_key_authority: Kew POWO Senna generic morphology; UT Austin Senna roemeriana; peer-reviewed extrafloral nectary study.
